llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed third-party image generation CLI integration that sends prompts and selected media to dLazy, with some install and credential-storage considerations for users to review.

dimensions.detail: Network calls, prompt submission, local media upload, and hosted result URLs are expected for a cloud image-generation service and are disclosed in the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned npm package or npx alternative for @dlazy/cli@1.2.2; the inspected package metadata showed no install hook, but it is still a third-party CLI install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include generic image-generation terms, which could activate the skill broadly, but the actual instructions are limited to the expected dlazy banana2 workflow and disclose remote API use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Authentication stores a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json unless the user chooses per-invocation environment variables; the artifact describes revocation and logout paths, but users on shared machines should be mindful of local config-file exposure.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Nano Banana 2.0 image generation/editing, and the runtime instructions consistently invoke the dLazy CLI for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you trust dLazy and are comfortable sending prompts and any referenced local images to its hosted service. Prefer npx or an environment variable if you do not want a persistent global CLI or saved API key, and avoid passing sensitive local media unless you intend to upload it.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad image-related triggers are present and overlap with the skill purpose; they are worth user awareness but do not show hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese skill file has the same broad trigger pattern; remote API and local file upload behavior are disclosed, so this remains guidance-level rather than a Review-level concern.
